_text: [fast-paced, energetic storyteller] In this world, every promise you make grows a *flower* out of your skin. [playful] Keep it, and it *blooms*. [amused] Break it, and it rots and *stinks*. [playful] You see, Linda ran the marathon she promised: a sunflower on her *knee*. [amused] Dad's sink promise? SIX years old. Dead tulip, on his ear. [mischievous] And the guy who said "I'll call you"? You can smell him from across the *mall*. [amazed] Then there's Derek: a THOUSAND perfect flowers, like a walking wedding cake. [playful] He's running for mayor, promising free pizza, a water park, and no more *Mondays*. [excited, building] And they bloom the *second* he says them. [playful, loud] Weirdly, bees never land on *him*. [urgent] But as mayor, he'll bulldoze Grandma's *beehives*. [determined] So you promise to save them, and a bud pops out of your *hand*. [mischievous] You borrow all her bees. In a SHOEBOX.
